cards.front: Where does safe arrival start, and what schedule guides vehicle upkeep?
cards.back: Safe arrival starts before ignition with both driver and car ready; steady upkeep saves cash, aids emergencies, and follows the owner manual schedule.

cards.front: How many braking systems must cars, trucks, and ATVs or UTVs carry, compared with motorcycles and mopeds?
cards.back: Cars, trucks, and ATVs or UTVs need twin braking systems, foot plus parking brake, while motorcycles and mopeds need at least one.

cards.front: Which brake symptoms send you to a mechanic?
cards.back: Weak braking, noisy brakes, odd brake odor, or a pedal sinking to the floor all send you to a mechanic.

cards.front: What governs upkeep timing, and what governs brake counts?
cards.back: Upkeep follows the owner manual schedule, while brake counts follow vehicle kind: twin systems for cars and ATVs, one for bikes.

cards.front: What are the brake warnings, and what is the only response?
cards.back: Noise, odor, and sinking pedals are the brake warnings, while a mechanic visit is the only response.

cards.front: How do you verify signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights?
cards.back: Verify signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights by walking around outside the car.

cards.front: What lights must every car, truck, and ATV or UTV carry?
cards.back: Every car, truck, and ATV or UTV carries two front headlights, left and right, plus at least one rear red lamp seen for five hundred feet and a white lamp lighting the rear plate.

cards.front: When are turn signals mandatory?
cards.back: Fitted turn signals must function, and signals are mandatory on all cars, trucks, and trailers wider than forty inches.

cards.front: What should you do about a crooked headlight?
cards.back: A crooked headlight wastes its beam and dazzles others, so night-vision trouble or constant oncoming flashes mean a mechanic should aim them.

cards.front: Why wash headlight, backup, brake, and tail lenses?
cards.back: Wash headlight, backup, brake, and tail lenses, since grime can slash their output by fifty percent.

cards.front: How do light checks and equipment counts differ?
cards.back: Light checks happen outside the car, while the equipment counts demand two headlights, one red rear lamp, and a plate lamp.

cards.front: What is the rule for fitted signals, and when do signals become mandatory?
cards.back: Any fitted signal must work, while signals become mandatory past forty inches of width.

cards.front: How do a crooked beam and a dimmed lens differ in their fix?
cards.back: Crooked beams need a mechanic re-aim, while dimmed lenses need only a wash.

cards.front: What does the manual say about cracked glass, windshield cleanliness, and washer fluid?
cards.back: Swap out cracked or broken glass that shatters easily and clouds sight, keep the windshield clean against sun and headlight glare, and top up washer fluid with antifreeze wash when frost threatens.

cards.front: What must you do about snow on windows and streaking wipers?
cards.back: Scrape snow, ice, and frost off every window, and keep the mandatory wipers wiping well with fresh blades when they streak.

cards.front: What does Iowa tint law require of the windshield and front side windows?
cards.back: Iowa tint law lets the windshield and front side windows pass at least seventy percent of light, with no medical exemption granted.

cards.front: How do you guard a clear view through the windshield?
cards.back: Guard a clear view by hanging nothing from the rearview mirror and pasting no decal clutter on the windshield.

cards.front: What happens to broken glass versus sound glass?
cards.back: Broken glass gets replaced, while sound glass gets cleaned and washed with antifreeze fluid.

cards.front: How do wipers and snow clearing differ from the tint limit?
cards.back: Wipers and snow clearing are driver chores, while the seventy-percent tint limit is the law with no medical pass.

cards.front: What do worn, bald, or unbalanced tires do, and what earns a mechanic visit?
cards.back: Worn, bald, or unbalanced tires stretch stopping distance, invite hydroplaning, wear faster, drink fuel, and fight steering and braking, while bouncing, wheel shake, or side-pull earns a mechanic visit.

cards.front: How do you set tire pressure?
cards.back: Inflate tires to spec, gauging pressure cold against the driver-door sticker or owner manual.

cards.front: How do you probe tire tread with a penny?
cards.back: Probe tread with a head-first penny; tread short of Lincoln crown top marks an unsafe tire due for replacement.

cards.front: How do the pressure check and the tread check differ?
cards.back: Pressure gets gauged cold against the door sticker, while tread gets probed with a head-first penny.

cards.front: How do bald tires and a bouncing car differ in what they mean?
cards.back: Bald tires stretch stops and invite slides, while bouncing and pulling send the car to a mechanic.

cards.front: What does steering that has gone stiff or slow to answer need?
cards.back: Steering gone stiff or slow to answer the wheel needs a mechanic inspection.

cards.front: What does endless bouncing after bumps or stops signal?
cards.back: Suspension steadies handling and comfort, so endless bouncing after bumps or stops signals worn shocks or parts.

cards.front: What do stiff steering and endless bouncing each point at?
cards.back: Stiff or lazy steering points at the steering gear, while endless bouncing points at shocks.

cards.front: Why must you never idle in a garage or sit in a running car with every window shut?
cards.back: Exhaust pipes away poison gas, muffles noise, and cools hot fumes, yet a leak can kill swiftly, so never idle in a garage or sit in a running car with every window shut.

cards.front: Why is idling in a garage never allowed?
cards.back: A leaky exhaust can kill in minutes, which is why idling in a garage is never allowed.

cards.front: What does a sour engine do, and what is the fix?
cards.back: A sour engine saps power, refuses starts, wastes fuel, fouls air, and may stall into traffic, so service it by the owner manual.

cards.front: What is the horn reserved for?
cards.back: The horn is a life-saving warner reserved strictly for warning others.

cards.front: What do a sour engine and the horn each call for?
cards.back: A sour engine gets serviced by the manual, while the horn gets used for warnings only.

cards.front: How far must the inside mirror reveal, and when are outside mirrors required?
cards.back: Your inside mirror must reveal two hundred feet astern; a load-blocked view demands an outside mirror, and vans must wear both outside mirrors.

cards.front: When should you set seat and mirrors for your own body?
cards.back: Dial in seat and mirrors for your own body before every drive, since fit governs control.

cards.front: How should you sit relative to the steering wheel?
cards.back: Sit spine-flat with at least ten inches of chest clearance from the wheel and the airbag aimed at your chest.

cards.front: Where should the wheel top sit, and how do shorter drivers keep the ten-inch gap?
cards.back: Keep the wheel top at or below shoulder height, plant your heel to pivot between pedals, and let shorter drivers add a cushion or pedal extenders to hold the ten-inch gap.

cards.front: Where should the head restraint sit?
cards.back: Float the head restraint level with the middle of your head.

cards.front: How do you set the inside mirror?
cards.back: Sit tall and frame the whole rear window in the inside mirror, your chief rearward eye.

cards.front: How do you set the left mirror?
cards.back: Tip your head to the left window and set the left mirror to just glimpse the car flank, a sliver that vanishes once you sit straight.

cards.front: How do you set the right mirror?
cards.back: Lean over the console and set the right mirror to just glimpse the right flank of the car.

cards.front: How do the rearview rule and the van rule differ?
cards.back: The rearview must show two hundred feet back, while vans must wear both outside mirrors regardless.

cards.front: How do the seat rule and the mirror method differ?
cards.back: The seat holds ten inches of chest clearance, while the mirrors get set by the lean-and-glimpse method.
